title: Edge coloring · LCA

verifiedRecords.bound: D^{O(√D log^{5/2}D)} · log* m line-graph oracle probes per queried edge
verifiedRecords.guarantee: Proper q=D+1 vertex coloring of L(G), hence q≤2Δ−1 edge coloring of G
verifiedRecords.sourceLocation: Theorem 5.1 (second case), Section 5; l=D+1 and d=1 on L(G)
verifiedRecords.notes: A direct theorem specialization, not an author-stated edge-LCA optimum. D is the degree of the line graph, not the degree Δ of G. The numerical exponent hidden in O(·) is not specified. The reviewed source provides no matching edge-LCA lower bound for this oracle.
verifiedRecords.quality: Proper edge coloring from a palette of D+1 colors, at most 2Δ−1
verifiedRecords.exactBound: D^{O(√D log^{5/2}D)} · log* m probes per query; palette allowance q=D+1≤2Δ−1
verifiedRecords.graph: Simple undirected graph G with m edges and maximum degree Δ; line graph L(G) has m vertices and maximum degree 2≤D≤2Δ−2
verifiedRecords.output: One color per queried edge, with all answers consistent with one proper coloring of G
verifiedRecords.oracle: Direct oracle access to vertices and neighborhoods of L(G), using the probe convention of Theorem 5.1; line-graph vertices are identified original edges
verifiedRecords.probability: Deterministic; all answered edge queries are correct and mutually consistent
verifiedRecords.adaptivity: Oblivious/stateless across queries; this does not assert that the probes within one query are nonadaptive
verifiedRecords.state: No information retained between queries; the same fixed oracle and identifiers define the implicit coloring
verifiedRecords.parameters: Known maximum line-graph degree D, a polynomial upper bound on m, and distinct O(log m)-bit identifiers for the line-graph vertices
verifiedRecords.theorem: Theorem 5.1, second case; Corollary 5.1, second case; Section 5, arXiv v2 printed pp. 13–14
derivation: Treat each original edge as a vertex of H=L(G), so |V(H)|=m.
For simple G, deg_H(uv)=deg_G(u)+deg_G(v)−2; hence D=max deg_H≤2Δ−2.
Give every H vertex the common list {1,…,D+1}, with only equal-color conflicts: l=D+1 and d=1, so l/d>D.
Apply Theorem 5.1 to H. A proper vertex coloring of H is a proper edge coloring of G.
assumptions: Direct line-graph oracle supplied; creating or simulating it from an ordinary adjacency-list or adjacency-matrix representation of G is outside this probe count
Simple graph; maximum line-graph degree D≥2; trivial D<2 cases are omitted
Use one fixed identifier assignment, oracle ordering and degree/size parameters for every query
Deterministic oblivious LCA; no stored state between queries
The resource is input probes per edge-color query, not total time or total cost for explicitly outputting every edge color
verifiedRecords.fixedDegree: For fixed D≥2, the degree factor is constant and the upper bound is O(log* m) probes per query; no tightness claim.
